long_biography.plain_text:
Before completing his economics degree, Jon Adgemis joined KPMG’s mergers-and-acquisitions practice. A period at Gresham Partners gave him public-markets experience before he returned to become a KPMG partner and national M&A leader. Advising private companies and family offices taught him how to source assets, structure capital and assess operational upside.

Adgemis applied that experience through JAGA, the investment group he founded after leaving advisory work. Its early strategy centred on vacant or underused commercial buildings that could be leased, repositioned or developed. Public Hospitality Group later extended the approach to pubs and hotels, pairing property refurbishment with venue operations and accommodation. The expansion was financed through substantial borrowing and ultimately failed, but it remains the defining expression of his move from adviser to principal.

proposed_details.existing_value:
The renowned 26.82m CRN yacht Hiilani, formerly known as Shirley Temple's Shirley B, is now under the ownership of Jon Adgemis, a 45-year-old Australian entrepreneur in the hospitality industry, as of April 2024.

The revelation of Mr. Adgemis's ownership of the yacht emerged from an article published in the Australian Financial Review on April 10, 2024. The article shed light on the yacht's ownership structure, revealing that it was registered under the company name The Yacht Pty Ltd. However, The Yacht Pty Ltd faced financial challenges and was placed into receivership in March 2024 due to the financial difficulties encountered by Mr. Adgemis's pub and hotel business, Public Hospitality Group. Subsequently, Mr. Adgemis swiftly regained control of The Yacht Pty Ltd. According to records from the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC), Mr. Adgemis is the sole shareholder of The Yacht Pty Ltd.
